dominant_participants: Trend followers, macro allocators, momentum-driven discretionary flows
economic_rationale: Gold trends most cleanly when persistence, liquidity support, and macro pressure align in the same direction.
label: bull_trend
market_mechanics: Breakouts are reinforced rather than faded, and validation quality improves because directional structure dominates noise.
typical_backdrop: Supportive USD and rates backdrop with persistent upside structure

dominant_participants: Systematic trend followers, directional macro sellers, hedgers
economic_rationale: Weak persistent structure forces gold research to distinguish between orderly unwind and true crisis behavior.
label: bear_unwind
market_mechanics: Negative trend persistence remains present, but not every downtrend carries the same validation penalty.
typical_backdrop: USD firmness or rates pressure with fading gold demand

dominant_participants: Carry allocators, reserve managers, low-turnover macro funds
economic_rationale: Low-volatility environments compress noise and allow slow information accumulation without crisis dislocation.
label: calm_carry
market_mechanics: Signals persist longer, but payoff asymmetry is smaller than in true bull trend expansion.
typical_backdrop: Calm policy environment and muted USD/rates shocks

dominant_participants: Forced de-risking, macro hedgers, crisis liquidity takers
economic_rationale: Crisis periods create large moves but poor research reliability unless treated as a separate state.
label: crisis_dislocation
market_mechanics: Volatility dominates signal quality, and contradictions increase because edge persistence degrades.
typical_backdrop: Stress episodes, geopolitical escalation, or policy disorder

dominant_participants: Macro funds, discretionary central-bank watchers, event-driven allocators
economic_rationale: Policy and cross-asset shocks change the information content of gold faster than trend-only taxonomies capture.
label: macro_transition
liquidity_profile: Tradable but sensitive to event timing
market_mechanics: Macro pressure and event stress alter the ranking of candidate hypotheses and explain why macro-only signals fail when isolated.
typical_backdrop: Policy repricing, real-yield shifts, DXY transitions

dominant_participants: Balanced macro books, range traders, hedging flows
economic_rationale: Most research time is spent outside explicit crisis or event transitions, so a broad compression state is required as the institutional default.
failure_modes: hidden transition starting inside the range
label: range_compression
market_mechanics: Signals are weaker than in bull trend expansion but more reliable than in crisis dislocation.
typical_backdrop: No dominant macro shock and no clean breakout persistence
